Secunda: adaptive music demo

Walk through the valley with the arrow keys (or WASD, or the pad). When you enter the enemy camp, the game asks the model for combat music; when you leave it, for exploration music again.

Exploration
Tension
Combat Score

Secunda cannot generate in real time on a CPU, so the demo plays clips generated in advance. Each clip continues a few seconds of a Skyrim or Witcher 3 passage with the controls of its state; only the generated part is played, never the original music. Expect codec artefacts: the model predicts 8 EnCodec codebooks (6 kbps).

Same prompt, different requests

Clips of experiment E2 generated by the Slakh-FT checkpoint. The first second is a real Slakh2100 test track (CC BY 4.0); the rest is generated with the requested controls. These prompts were chosen because their measured tension change is closest to the median over prompts: they are typical examples, not the best ones.
